records.title: Sand mining in the Mekong Delta revisited — current scales of local sediment deficits
records.dateEvidence: Publisher citation metadata and article header: 2019 Nov 28
records.location: Tien River between Sa Dec and the Tien–Co Chien bifurcation near Vinh Long
records.summary: Jordan and colleagues used repeat bathymetric surveys and sediment measurements along about 20 km of the Tien River, between Sa Dec and the bifurcation near Vinh Long. They estimated 2018 sand extraction at 4.64 ± 0.31 million m³/year within that study reach. The paper compares this with reported statistics of 17.77 million m³/year across the delta’s channels and argues that reported extraction was too conservative. Natural sediment supply did not compensate for extraction in the study area.
records.limitations: The extraction estimate concerns one surveyed reach and 2018. It is not a current delta-wide total. Causal interpretations and uncertainties remain those of the paper.
records.editorialStatus: Pilot — awaiting owner review

records.title: Geography of Sand and Gravel Mining in the Lower Mekong River. First Survey and Impact Assessment
records.authors: Jean-Paul Bravard, Marc Goichot and Stéphane Gaillot
records.studyPeriod: 2011 for Lao PDR, Thailand and Cambodia; 2012 for Viet Nam
records.location: Lower Mekong main stem and two delta channels; upper basin and tributaries excluded
records.summary: Bravard, Goichot and Gaillot surveyed aggregate operators along the Lower Mekong in Lao PDR, Thailand, Cambodia and Viet Nam. They report 34.48 million m³ of extracted sediment, equivalent to 55.2 million tonnes using a dry-sand density of 1.6 tonnes/m³; sand accounted for about 90%, or 31 million m³. The underlying country observations concern 2011 except Viet Nam, which concerns 2012. The authors identify extraction as an important pressure on the river’s sediment budget.
records.limitations: Operator declarations may underestimate extraction by an unknown factor. China, tributaries and most delta channels were not surveyed. The mixed observation years are retained; the totals are historical survey estimates.
records.editorialStatus: Pilot — awaiting owner review

records.title: The Viet Nam Mekong Delta Sand Budget
records.authors: Project partners led by Deltares, supported by WWF
records.dateEvidence: No reliable publication date identified on the project page. The project period is not used as a publication date.
records.studyPeriod: 2022–2023 project; observations from 2022 and a vision to 2040
records.location: Viet Nam Mekong Delta
records.summary: The project page describes a delta-wide sand budget combining field measurements, numerical modelling and stakeholder consultation. It reports extraction of roughly 35–55 million m³/year, against incoming sand flux of 2–4 million m³/year and natural outgoing flux of 0–0.6 million m³/year. The estimated mobile sand stock is 367–550 million m³. Its projection that this stock could be depleted within a decade depends on future demand and the study’s assumptions. The project ran in 2022–2023; those years are kept separate from the unverified page publication date.
records.limitations: This record represents the project’s overview page, not an independent audit or a full review of the linked technical reports. Stock and annual flux are different quantities. Text extraction joined some words; no image-only values were inferred.
records.editorialStatus: Pilot — awaiting owner review

records.title: Uncovering the Mekong Sand Debt
records.dateEvidence: No reliable publication date identified in the page text or retrieved publisher metadata.
records.studyPeriod: Not specified as a single observation period
records.location: Viet Nam Mekong Delta; upstream sediment supply discussed as context
records.summary: Deltares explains sand debt as extraction exceeding replenishment in the Mekong Delta. The project overview distinguishes sediment trapping by upstream dams from downstream sand removal and describes a budget accounting for incoming sand, internal movement, existing stock, extraction and outgoing sand. It presents this framework as support for resource-management decisions in the Viet Nam Mekong Delta.
records.limitations: This is an institutional project account. The page contains an apparent inconsistency in its percentage attribution of salinity change; those figures are excluded here pending clarification. It overlaps with the Sand Budget project and is not an independent extraction event.
records.editorialStatus: Pilot — awaiting owner review

records.title: Extent of illegal sand mining in the Mekong Delta
records.location: Viet Nam Mekong Delta
records.summary: The researchers defined illegal extraction as estimated actual mining above provincial allowable rates. They estimated 16.7 million m³/year in 2013 and 15.5 million m³/year in 2018–2020, while allowable extraction increased from 11.5 to 15.1 million m³/year.
records.limitations: This is the paper’s calculated estimate relative to provincial allowable rates, not a determination about individual operators.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: Sand-mining-driven reduction in Tonle Sap Lake’s critical flood pulse
records.location: Tonle Sap–Mekong system and Mekong Delta
records.summary: The modelling study attributes an estimated 40–50% reduction in Tonle Sap reverse flow between 1998 and 2018 to riverbed lowering associated with sand mining and upstream sediment trapping. It projects a 69% reduction by 2038 relative to 1998 under further lowering.
records.limitations: These are modelled estimates and scenario-dependent projections; the paper considers both mining and upstream sediment trapping.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: A Thirst for Sand
records.authors: Lê Đình Tuyển, Pratch Rujivanarom, Teng Yalirozy and Lay Sopheavotey
records.location: Mekong region, including Dong Thap province, Viet Nam
records.summary: The regional report connects construction demand, sand extraction, erosion and livelihoods. In Dong Thap, a resident describes relocating twice as her riverbank eroded. It cites satellite-based Cambodian extraction estimates of 24 million tonnes in 2016 and 59 million tonnes in 2020.
records.limitations: The article synthesizes reporting and previously published research. The extraction figures are attributed to that research and should not be added to its separate archive record.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: Life’s no beach for Thais affected by sand mining
records.location: Had Hae, That Phanom district, Nakhon Phanom, and Bueng Kan, Thailand; Vientiane prefecture, Lao PDR
records.summary: Reporting from the Thai Mekong describes concerns that Had Hae beach in That Phanom district has shrunk. A municipal official attributes the loss to excessive extraction; the article also discusses upstream dams, sediment supply, fragmented oversight and sand mined in Lao PDR for Thai markets.
records.limitations: Community and official accounts are attributed. The report does not isolate mining’s contribution from other drivers of beach change.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: Mekong Delta pays a high price from sand mining
records.location: Long Phu Thuan, Dong Thap and Binh Thuan 1 hamlet, Vinh Long, Viet Nam
records.summary: The report documents residents’ accounts of erosion and sand extraction in Dong Thap and Vinh Long. It reports that a December 2022 collapse in Binh Thuan 1 affected 13 houses and left 109 people without homes; provincial authorities subsequently suspended nearby mining.
records.limitations: Attribution of individual erosion events to mining requires independent assessment. The article also describes other pressures on the delta.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: Assessment of the Impact of Sand Mining on Bottom Morphology in the Mekong River in An Giang Province, Vietnam, Using a Hydro-Morphological Model with GPU Computing
records.location: Tan Chau town, An Giang province, Viet Nam
records.summary: The authors model riverbed change along the Mekong near Tan Chau for 1999–2019, including mining at Tan An during 2002–2006 and later activity near Vinh Hoa. They report a modelled erosion channel of −23 m in 2006 and a subsequent recovery rate of 0.25 m/year for the described period.
records.limitations: These are site- and model-specific results. The abstract’s wording on erosion speed is ambiguous; consult the complete study for scenario comparisons.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: 'Houses On The River Will Fall': Cambodia's Sand Mining Threatens Vital Mekong
records.location: Kdey Takoy temple and Phnom Penh, Cambodia
records.summary: NPR reports on sand dredging, construction demand and riverbank concerns near Phnom Penh. A monk at Kdey Takoy temple describes a bank collapse while dredging occurred offshore; the article includes both an official’s account of economic and navigation benefits and environmentalists’ concerns.
records.limitations: The monk’s account and other causal claims are attributed; the report is not an independent geomorphic investigation.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: ‘No Authority Ever Paid Attention’: Mekong Villagers Confront Sand Dredgers, Distrust Lingers
records.location: Thmey village, Prey Veng province, Cambodia
records.summary: Residents of Thmey village describe confronting dredgers and allege that dredging damaged riverbanks and exceeded permitted areas. One resident says the river moved from about 30 m to 10 m behind her home. Officials previously maintained that operations were licensed and within project boundaries; the article reports a disputed 1.39-billion-tonne licensed amount for Mekong and Bassac extraction.
records.limitations: Allegations, company responses, the official account and the reported licence amount remain attributed. A licence amount is not measured extraction.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: Sand mining far outpaces natural supply in a large alluvial river
records.location: Lower Mekong River, Cambodia
records.summary: Using monthly PlanetScope imagery and sand-barge tracking, the authors estimate extraction increased from 24 million tonnes (17–32 million) in 2016 to 59 million tonnes (41–75 million) in 2020. They report median reach-wide bed incision of −0.26 m/year for 2013–2019.
records.limitations: These are satellite-derived estimates with reported bounds for the Cambodian study area, not unique boats or direct measurements of all mining.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: Precarious livelihoods at the intersection of fishing and sand mining in Cambodia
records.authors: Furqan Asif and Lukas Van Arragon
records.location: Cambodian coastal fishing villages and Mekong sand-mining industry
records.summary: The authors combine qualitative research from Cambodian coastal fishing villages and the Mekong sand-mining industry. They argue that the interaction can support some livelihoods while undermining others, connecting precarious labour to environmental change and fisheries.
records.limitations: The two underlying studies cover different settings, including coastal fishing villages; this is not a basin-wide quantitative extraction estimate.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: Uncovering the lack of awareness of sand mining impacts on riverbank erosion among Mekong Delta residents: insights from a comprehensive survey
records.location: Bassac River, Vietnamese Mekong Delta
records.summary: Researchers interviewed residents along the Bassac River about sand mining and riverbank erosion. They report that respondents generally perceived environmental harm, while awareness of mining’s role in bank instability was limited and differed among those directly affected by collapse.
records.limitations: The results describe perceptions among study participants; they should not be generalized to all Mekong Delta residents without considering the study design.
records.editorialStatus: Source reviewed; owner review pending

records.title: Cambodia’s insatiable appetite for river sand
records.location: Kandal province, Cambodia
records.summary: Teng Yalirozy and Lay Sopheavotey report from Kandal on night dredging, residents’ concerns about bank collapse, and alleged regulatory corruption; they cite satellite-based research estimating Cambodian extraction rose from 24 million tons in 2016 to 59 million tons in 2020 and discuss possible effects on Tonle Sap flows.
records.limitations: The residents’ causal claims and some corruption allegations are reported rather than independently proven; the extraction estimates are attributed to a cited study, not newly calculated by the reporters.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: In the Mekong Delta, sand mining means lost homes and fortunes
records.location: An Giang, Dong Thap, Can Tho, Vinh Long and Soc Trang, Viet Nam
records.summary: Lê Đình Tuyển reports on households affected by erosion and traces permitted extraction across five delta provinces; residents blame dredging for collapses, while experts attribute erosion to reduced sediment from dams and excessive mining in Cambodia and Viet Nam.
records.limitations: The article reports residents’ attribution and expert assessments but cannot isolate mining from dams, flow change, and other erosion drivers; figures are based on official records and sources cited in the report.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: Viet Nam’s Mekong Delta is running out of sand. What’s next?
records.location: Viet Nam Mekong Delta
records.summary: The report examines a WWF Viet Nam assessment, reporting annual extraction of 35–55 million cubic metres against 2–4 million naturally replenishable and a possible 2035 depletion date; it also reports post-arrest shortages and construction impacts in the delta.
records.limitations: The figures and projections are attributed to WWF’s assessment; the article does not reproduce its full methods. Publication date verified in publisher metadata.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: In Cambodia, Exposing the Ecological Scars of Sand Mining
records.location: Phnom Penh and Kandal province, Cambodia
records.summary: The report describes extraction feeding Phnom Penh’s construction demand, documents barges on the Tonle Bassac, and connects dredging to bank collapse, deaths, and damaged houses; it also reports Mother Nature Cambodia’s investigation of export and revenue discrepancies.
records.limitations: The fetched page contains a short report plus contextual material and some claims attributed to activists and experts; it does not provide a comprehensive official extraction dataset.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: In Cambodia, sand mining is big business -- but it comes at a price
records.location: Phnom Penh and downstream, Cambodia
records.summary: Fred de Sam Lazaro’s broadcast report and transcript examine Cambodian dredging for construction sand, government claims of economic benefit, activists’ allegations that mining continues, and land loss around Phnom Penh and downstream sites.
records.limitations: This is a television report/transcript with selected interviews and field observations, not a basin-wide audit; several causal and governance claims are attributed to interviewees.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: Dramatic Photos Show How Sand Mining Threatens a Way of Life in Southeast Asia
records.location: Tien River, Dong Thap, Viet Nam
records.summary: The photo-report documents a resident’s home collapse on the Tien River and identifies nearby dredging boats and pumps as the visible sand-extraction pressure; it links demand for concrete to damage in the Mekong Delta.
records.limitations: The page is a short photo-led report and does not state a full methodology or quantify extraction; its causal framing is based on observed dredging and reported local experience.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: Cát nạo lên, tiền đổ xuống - Kỳ 1: Xung đột cát - sạt lở
records.location: An Giang and Mekong Delta, Viet Nam
records.summary: Đình Tuyển’s first Vietnamese investigation uses provincial, national geology, and agriculture data to examine conflict between eroding communities and sand miners, the scale of extraction, and alleged profiteering and regulatory responses.
records.limitations: The source is in Vietnamese and the summary here is a translation; the article describes associations between mining and erosion but does not claim mining is the only driver. Translation and summary await native-language editorial review.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: Hết cát - Thử thách sống còn cho Đồng bằng sông Cửu Long
records.location: Can Tho and Vinh Long, Viet Nam
records.summary: The second investigation reports active bucket dredging near Cồn Sơn, residents’ repeated relocations and protests, limited public mine data, and the delta’s sediment deficit; it includes community and authority perspectives on balancing construction demand and erosion.
records.limitations: The source is in Vietnamese and the summary is translated; reported residents’ claims about particular dredgers and erosion are not independently verified in the article. Translation and summary await native-language editorial review.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: Cát nạo lên, tiền đổ xuống: Sông sạt lở, bờ biển thụt lùi
records.location: Viet Nam Mekong Delta
records.summary: The third investigation examines governance and alternatives, reporting unstable supply and prices, expert estimates of annual sediment inflow versus mining and outflow, and proposals for a sand bank and more transparent basin-scale management.
records.limitations: The source is in Vietnamese and this is a translation; estimates are attributed to MRC, WWF, and named experts, and the article does not independently validate those estimates. Translation and summary await native-language editorial review.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: ‘Hungry river’ phenomenon to blame for severe erosion of Mekong River banks in Laos
records.location: Bolikhamxay, Saravan and Vientiane area, Lao PDR; Thai Mekong bank
records.summary: RFA reports expert and official accounts linking severe Mekong bank erosion in Laos to sediment depletion from upstream dams and sand dredging. It gives reported erosion lengths in Bolikhamxay and Saravan, includes a Thai community-network view that Thai banks are also affected, and reports an official attributing erosion to sand dredging while calling water-fluctuation causes unresolved. An official reported severe erosion along at least 73 km of a 179 km Mekong bank reach in Bolikhamxay, of which 21 km had retaining walls.
records.limitations: The report covers erosion broadly, with dams and other factors alongside dredging. Its causal claims are attributed to experts or officials, and it does not quantify sand removed or establish the relative contribution of dredging versus dams, deforestation or climate variability.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: More than 100 million tons of sand mined from Lower Mekong, experts say
records.location: Lower Mekong basin; Cambodia and Viet Nam estimates
records.summary: RFA reports experts’ estimate that Cambodia and Vietnam together extract about 100 million metric tons of sand annually, and says older basin estimates included about 7 million tons from Laos. It reports researchers’ finding that extraction is widespread, under-monitored and associated with sediment loss, riverbed erosion and salinity risks, and notes the Mekong River Commission’s basin-wide sediment-management response.
records.limitations: The researchers did not calculate current figures for Laos or Thailand; the 100-million-ton estimate excludes Laos and upstream areas. The article is based largely on an expert seminar and cited studies rather than original field measurements by RFA.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: Grain drain, Laos' sand mining damaging the Mekong
records.location: Vientiane area, Lao PDR
records.summary: AFP reports from Laos that industrial-scale dredging around Vientiane supplies sand for construction, including Chinese-backed development, while affecting the riverbed, fishermen and farmers. It describes company and official accounts, WWF’s warning that the rate is unsustainable, and the lack of Laos government extraction figures.
records.limitations: This is a republished AFP report rather than a Yahoo-original article. It provides no measured extraction total for Laos; the Lao official declined to provide figures, and environmental impacts are reported through interviewees and expert attribution.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: The Environmental Costs of Sand Mining on the Mekong
records.location: Simaogang, Yunnan, China
records.summary: Sixth Tone reporters Luc Forsyth and Denise Hruby describe commercial dredging at Simaogang on the Lancang, including operators' reported extraction capacity and the provincial restrictions in ecological hotspots; the article links sediment removal to basin-wide ecological concerns.
records.limitations: The report is a field feature rather than a systematic basin inventory; its capacity and price figures are attributed to interviewees or cited sources, and it does not quantify Myanmar or the full upper basin.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: Mekong river sand mining is a crumbling castle
records.location: ASEAN Mekong countries, regional scope
records.summary: Lilla Szabó argues that sand extraction across the five ASEAN Mekong countries, including Myanmar, is faster than natural renewal and requires transboundary governance. The explainer proposes coordinated monitoring, restrictions at vulnerable sites, and output/export taxation rather than an absolute ban.
records.limitations: This is an authored policy explainer, not an on-the-ground investigation; it synthesizes linked studies and gives no Myanmar-specific site, operator, or measured volume.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: River bank instability from unsustainable sand mining in the lower Mekong River
records.location: Lower Mekong River
records.summary: Hackney and co-authors use field/channel observations and morphodynamic analysis to link extraction that exceeds replenishment with bed lowering and increased bank instability in the lower Mekong.
records.limitations: Abstract-only access; selected reaches and modelled/observed bank instability do not constitute a basin-wide causal experiment.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending

records.title: New systematically measured sand mining budget for the Mekong Delta reveals rising trends and significant volume underestimations
records.publisher: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation (Elsevier)
records.location: Tien River and Vietnamese Mekong Delta
records.summary: Using satellite boat metrics calibrated against bathymetric surveys on about 100 km of the Tien River, the authors estimate that delta-wide sand extraction rose from 38 million m³/year in 2015 to 47 million m³/year in 2020; the six-year total was estimated at 254 million m³.
records.limitations: Publisher abstract and highlights read; the delta-wide estimates extrapolate from surveyed reaches and depend on satellite detection and calibration.
records.editorialStatus: AI-assisted source review; owner review pending
